title: Book club
topic: A friend counts inclusive pages read tonight and remaining pages left in a novel
blurb: A friend is pacing the last chapters before Thursday's book club.
prompt: A friend just sent this in the group chat. Tap a line if something doesn't add up, or let it pass.

segments.label: Tonight
segments.text: Trying to finish the novel before book club Thursday — read from the top of page 84 to the bottom of page 147 tonight.

segments.label: The tally
segments.text: Knocked out 64 pages in one sitting.

segments.label: What's left
segments.text: The book ends on page 275, so 128 pages left — two more nights at this pace and I'm done.

segments.label: The brag
segments.text: Might actually show up knowing the ending.

conclusion: Pages 84–147 is 64 pages, leaving 128 pages to 275 — two more nights at this pace.

diagnosis: Starting on page 84 means you already read 84 pages earlier, not 83, which throws off the remaining count.
Reading 'from the top of 84 through the bottom of 147' counts both ends twice when you also add +1 on line 2.
Chapter breaks leave half-empty pages, so page 84 to 147 isn't a real 64-page pace.
If you stopped at the bottom of page 147, tomorrow starts on 147, not 148.
fix: Count pages 84 through 147 as 147 − 84 = 63 pages so you don't double-count the ends.
Note that you've read 84 pages before tonight, not 83.
Start tomorrow's count at page 147 so you don't lose a page between sessions.
Time yourself by chapters instead of page numbers.

diagnosis: 147 minus 84 is 63 pages, not 64 — adding 1 double-counts page 84.
Counting both page 84 and page 147 means adding 2, so tonight was 65 pages.
147 minus 84 is 53 plus 1 = 54 pages; you mis-subtracted the tens digit.
You only add 1 when counting from page 1, not when starting mid-book on page 84.
fix: Fix tonight's tally to 65 pages since both endpoints are included.
Drop the '+1' rule whenever you start after page 1.

diagnosis: By your own rule from line 2, 275 minus 147 needs +1 too — that's 129 pages left, so two nights of 64 still leaves 1 page.
275 minus 148 is 127 pages left, not 128, because you already finished page 147.
At 63 pages a night (from line 2), 128 pages takes three nights, not two.
275 minus 147 is 138 pages left, which is more than two 64-page nights.
fix: Add 1 to 275 − 147 to get 129 pages left — you'll need an extra page on night two.
Subtract 275 − 148 = 127 pages left since page 147 is already done.
Plan on three nights since 128 ÷ 63 is slightly over two.
Fix the subtraction to 138 pages left and budget 69 pages a night.

diagnosis: If you've actually got 129 pages left and only read 64 a night, you'll still miss the final page.
Reading 63 pages a night leaves 2 pages unread after two nights, right on the ending.
Book club is Thursday and 'tonight' could be Wednesday, leaving only one night, not two.
Two nights at 54 pages is 108 pages, leaving you 20 pages short of the ending.
fix: Read 65 pages on one of the next two nights so you cover all 129 pages.
Bump your target to 64 real pages instead of 63 so you don't miss the last two pages.
Check the calendar — make sure you actually have two nights before Thursday.
Read 70 pages a night to make sure you hit page 275 with room to spare.
